parts.latex: Explain why the percentage of scores between 46 and 70 is twice your answer to part (a).
By using the values in the table above, find an approximate minimum score that a candidate would need to be placed in the top $10\%$ of the candidates.
parts.note: Top 10% score found from a z-table of normal probabilities, which is not in the 2024 course.

solutions.latex:
Find the $z$-score of 70.

$$\begin{aligned} z &= \dfrac{70-58}{15} \\ &= 0.8 \end{aligned}$$

From the table, $P(Z<0.8)=0.7881$.

The area between the mean and $z=0.8$ is

$$\begin{aligned} P &= 0.7881-0.5 \\ &= 0.2881 \end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore\ 28.81\%$$
criteria: Finds the $z$-score corresponding to 70, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The $z$-score for 46 is $-0.8$.

By symmetry about the mean, the area between 46 and 58 equals the area between 58 and 70.

So the percentage of scores between 46 and 70 is twice $28.81\%$.

The top $10\%$ starts at the 90th percentile. From the table, $P(Z<1.3)\approx 0.9$, so $z=1.3$.

$$1.3=\dfrac{x-58}{15}$$

$$x=77.5$$

$$\therefore\ \text{Approximate minimum score}=77$$

Answers could include: 78

solutions.latex:
For a normal distribution, about $95\%$ of scores lie within 2 standard deviations of the mean. So the mean is the midpoint of 59 and 107.
$$\text{mean}=\dfrac{59+107}{2}=83$$
The distribution is symmetric, so the modal score equals the mean, $83$.

The distance from 59 to 107 is $4$ standard deviations.
$$\begin{aligned} 4\sigma &= 107-59 = 48 \\ \sigma &= 12 \end{aligned}$$
The range of a normal distribution is not given by the interval 59 to 107, so the range of $48$ in A and B is not correct.

Hence modal score $=83$ and standard deviation $=12$, which is option C.
